newsitem.title: UK: Britain seeks company input on windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: Britain seeks company input on windfall tax.

text.p: Britain's Treasury department asked on Tuesday for representations from companies over the government's proposed one-off "windfall" tax on privatised utilities.
In a statement, paymaster general Geoffrey Robinson said he would be "willing to take into account any representations from companies on (the windfall tax's) technical operation".
Representations should be made by the end of May, the statement said.
Details of the proposed levy, aimed at financing a three billion stg programme to help young and long-term unemployed, will be announced in Chancellor Gordon Brown's first budget.
